sentences.text: Brachylophosaurus is a genus of dinosaur belonging to the family Hadrosauridae and the class Ornithischia.
This dinosaur possessed a distinctive flat, paddle-like bony crest on the back of its skull that was solid and massive rather than hollow.
Its upper jaw bone was elongated in the front section, and it possessed dental batteries containing hundreds of stacked teeth to process vegetation.
Adult Brachylophosaurus reached a length of at least 9 meters, with some estimates suggesting a maximum length of 11 meters and a weight of 7 metric tons.
Soft tissue casts on fossils generally lay close to the bones, revealing muscles about six centimeters thick around the right shoulder and fingers encased in a shared sheath resembling a mitten.
A famous specimen nicknamed 'Leonardo' was identified by the Guinness Book of World Records as the 'Best Preserved Dinosaur'.
The 'Leonardo' specimen showed evidence of parasitism by small, needle-like worms with fine bristles found in its stomach.
A massive bonebed containing 800 specimens of Brachylophosaurus was found in the Judith River Formation of Montana.
Brachylophosaurus was first named by Charles Mortram Sternberg in 1953, with the type species designated as Brachylophosaurus canadensis.
The type specimen, catalogued as CMN 8893, was collected by Sternberg in 1936 from Dinosaur Provincial Park in Alberta, Canada.
The specific quarry where the type specimen was found was lost for over 20 years before being rediscovered in 2001 and designated Q103.
Additional specimens, including skeleton MOR 794 discovered in 1994 and a specimen nicknamed 'Leonardo' found in 2000, were located during expeditions led by Nate Murphy near Malta, Montana.
Brachylophosaurus was a generalist herbivore that acted as both a browser and grazer, but primarily browsed based on stomach contents.
Despite examining over 10,000 fossils, tumors were found only in Brachylophosaurus and closely related genera.
Brachylophosaurus belongs to the subfamily Brachylophosaurini.
Brachylophosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically within the Campanian stage between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
Fossils in the Dinosaur Park Formation may represent individuals that died while migrating, and the dinosaur may have inhabited upland areas where it nested or fed.
John R. Horner named a Montana specimen Brachylophosaurus goodwini, but it is debated whether this is a synonym of B. canadensis or a distinct member of the Brachylophosaurini tribe.
It is also debated whether the crest was used for pushing contests, as some researchers suggest it but others doubt it was strong enough.
